title: Unenforced Memory Alignment/Layout Warnings
pattern: Prose comments warning of extreme safety or segmentation faults resulting from manual pointer or byte-layout alignments.
why_bad: Fragile and dangerous. Humans are poor at enforcing byte alignments manually across updates. Modern compiled languages provide explicit memory layout attributes to enforce alignment safely at compile-time.
detection: Warning comments regarding pointer or memory-alignment bounds placed above bitwise arithmetic on offsets or manual byte padding.
counterexample: Compiler-enforced layout via `#[repr(align(16))]`, making misalignment unrepresentable without any warning prose.
fix: Replace manual bit-manipulation and warning comments with compiler-level memory alignment attributes like `#[repr(align(...))]`.
source: Steve McConnell, *Code Complete* (2004), Chapter 32 ("Don't comment tricky code; rewrite it").
